honest_framing: RESETS MAKE THE PROBLEM EASIER than reset-free learning. With a reset every experiment starts from the known start state, and the classical theory of N-complete test suites applies. v0.64.0 failed without resets; this study does not fix reset-free certification, which stays Open.

The certificate here is NOT Brute's SAT engine. It is a new host-agnostic module, brute.certify/32r: an L*-style learner with a Vasilevskii-Chow N-complete test suite (Vasilevskii 1973, Chow 1978). The guarantee is that theorem, conditional on the declared N, on resets returning the decoder to its start state, and on settled readings being correct.
These are small real targets of 6 to 13 Moore states, not a capability leap. Noise is injected by the adapter, not real.
question: Q1 (main): do resets fix the v0.64.0 failure on the same three real decoders at the same declared N 12? Q2 (stretch): does it scale to euc_jp (13 states, N 16)? Q3 (held out): gb18030 (8 states, N 12).

interface.public_only: experiments/targets_069.py: each query word gets a FRESH codecs.getincrementaldecoder(codec)('replace') object (the reset), then one .decode(bytes([b])) per letter, final=False. interface.reading: as plan 068: 2 bits of the str returned by the latest decode() call (non-empty, contains U+FFFD); (0,0) for a fresh object. Re-reads return the cached last reading (state-preserving).
interface.machine: Moore machine over the target bytes, state = (undecoded buffer, class of last output), start = fresh decoder

api.module: brute/api/certify32r.py (NEW file; no existing brute/ file changes)
api.name: brute.certify/32r
api.algorithm: observation tree keyed by words from reset; L* table (S prefix-closed access words, E suffixes with the empty word first; rows over S and S.Sigma); close by moving a new row into S; hypothesis H = rows of S; then the Vasilevskii-Chow suite S . Sigma^{<= N-n+1} . E, words visited in an order shuffled by random.Random(seed) per depth; the first word on which the tree disagrees with H is a counterexample and ALL its suffixes join E (Maler-Pnueli), then close again. Every queried word is run from a fresh decoder and every prefix reading is recorded.

labels.ID: H has n <= N states and every suite word agrees: by the Vasilevskii-Chow theorem every machine with at most N states that agrees with the observations is equivalent to H
labels.EXCEEDS_N: the table has more than N distinct rows: the target has more than N states (exact refutation of the declaration)

api.noise: arm S: each NEW tree node (one per new prefix) is read one noisy reading at a time until every bit settles at threshold certify20s.threshold(t, eps_bar, delta, 2), t = index of the settled observation (union bound: all settled readings correct with probability >= 1 - delta). Cached nodes are not re-read.
api.host_agnostic: no I/O, os, subprocess, threads, network or global state (GHOST69 checks the AST)

arms.S: certify/32r at injected iid bit noise eps 0.30 (eps_bar 0.35, delta 0.001; worlds_065.Noise)
